# Design Pressures {#sec-pressures-ch}

Every solar design is pushed from several directions at once. The price a developer bid pushes toward a simple rectangle of panels. A tractor that has to fit underneath pushes the panels up and the rows apart. A neighbor's view pushes for a screen along the road, a buyer's scorecard pushes for the credits it counts, and a county ordinance pushes for its setbacks. This lexicon calls these forces the **[design pressures](terminology.qmd#term-design-pressures)**: nine of them, each pushing the design in its own direction, and each with someone arguing for it in good faith.

![Nine pressures bearing on one site at once, arranged by the direction each pushes. The two colored groups never meet, because the three whose direction is decided by the site, the buyer, or the county sit in the gray wedges between them.](../figures/fig_design_pressures.svg){#fig-design-pressures}

## The nine pressures {#sec-pressures}

Three pressures push toward restoration, three push against it, and which way the remaining three push depends on the site, the buyer, or the county. Restorative goals is the pressure this lexicon exists to advance, but it is still one force among nine, and it loses to the other eight more often than not.

::: {.pressure-table}
| Pressure | What it asks for | Which way it pushes |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **[Restorative goals](terminology.qmd#term-restorative-goals)** | Wider rows, mixed ground cover, and a plan covering all thirty years | **Toward.** The one this lexicon argues for |
| **[Community acceptance and benefit](terminology.qmd#term-community-acceptance)** | A say early enough to change the design, and something paid back: tax revenue, subscriptions, local hiring, part-ownership | **Toward,** mostly. Paying people without asking them first buys resentment, not consent [@crawford2022] |
| **[End-of-life responsibility](terminology.qmd#term-end-of-life)** | Removable foundations, less digging, funded [decommissioning](terminology.qmd#term-decommissioning) | **Toward.** Every graded acre is soil somebody has to rebuild later |
| **[Agricultural production](terminology.qmd#term-agricultural-production)** | Clearance for a tractor, room to turn, something worth growing underneath | **Both.** It is why there are sheep under the panels, and why there is no prairie |
| **[Grid and market demands](terminology.qmd#term-grid-market)** | The power contract, the renewable-energy credits, a grid connection the queue will deliver | **Both.** A buyer's scorecard can plant habitat on a thousand sites, or lock the wrong seed mix into all of them |
| **[Policy and permission](terminology.qmd#term-policy-permission)** | The permitting path, prime-farmland and setback rules, and the subsidies that decide what pays | **Both.** California's groundwater law pays a grower to retire irrigated ground. Iowa's ethanol mandate pays a grower to keep planting it |
| **[Operations and maintenance](terminology.qmd#term-operations-maintenance)** | Cover that is simple to mow, or gravel that never grows, for thirty years | **Away, then toward.** Natives cost more for three years and less every year after |
| **[Energy yield](terminology.qmd#term-energy-yield)** | Panels packed close, tilted to the sun, low, and edge to edge | **Away,** though plants underneath keep modules cooler and cool modules make more power [@merheb2025] |
| **[Cost and financing](terminology.qmd#term-cost-financing)** | Standard racking, simple rectangles, and a project big enough to raise money against | **Away.** Anything unusual costs more, and the paperwork does not shrink with the project |
: The nine pressures and the direction each one pushes. The third column is a direction, not a verdict on anyone advocating it. {#tbl-pressures}
:::

## Where the pressures collide {#sec-conflicts}

Whatever a design leaves unresolved is its [design tension](terminology.qmd#term-design-tension). **No combination of lever settings brings it to zero**, because the nine cannot all be satisfied and the project still has to get built. What varies is how much tension is left, and who carries it. The hardest collision is between two pressures that both push toward restoration. Established habitat and rebuilt soil take years to create, and they do not come out cleanly when the array does, so a project designed to leave no trace and a project designed to heal the ground are not always the same project. The combinations that leave the least tension get built again and again, and those are the [archetypes](archetypal-forms.qmd) of Chapter 7.

## How the pressures vary by region {#sec-regionality}

The same nine pressures act on every site, but they carry different weight in every region. Shade that relieves a water-stressed crop in Arizona can cut corn yields in Ohio. Across 367 paired observations, the turning point sits near 30 °C air temperature [@merheb2025]. Retiring irrigated ground above a depleted aquifer has no equivalent in a county whose crops run on rain. Six factors shift the weights: sun and cloud, the grid operator, aridity, latitude, the cropping system, and irrigation. The words travel between regions and the weights do not, which is why this lexicon argues for an aim and leaves the dimensions to the site.

::: {.callout-tip .running-example icon=false title="At Rabbit Hills"}
Energy yield set the array's shape: low panels in close rows, the layout a developer builds anywhere. Agricultural production is the pressure that kept the sheep on the pasture, and the low clearance settled which animals it could be: sheep, not cattle. The measurements in Chapter 6 suggest that neither pressure had to give up much. The flock gets shade and forage under the panels, and the ground beneath the array is grazed rather than mown.
:::
